newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi expects record 1997 sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Audi expects record 1997 sales, profit.

text.p: German luxury carmaker Audi AG, a unit of Volkswagen AG, said on Wednesday it expected to post record sales and earnings in 1997, thanks in part to strong demand for its new A6 saloon.
Audi said at its annual general meeting that it expected 1997 sales to top 20 billion marks and to also report a higher pre-tax profit than the 1996 level of 862 million marks.
Audi also said it expected to sell more than 500,000 vehicles around the world during the year and expected first-half sales to rise 16 percent to 10.8 billion marks.
Franz-Josef Paefgen, who took over as Audi management board chairman at the meeting, said global vehicle sales during the first half of the year were up 12.9 percent to 277,000 units.
But Audi, noting its production capacity was fully utilised, said it expected slower sales growth in the second half of the year compared with the first half.
Sales in Germany were up 11.7 percent during the six-month period, which boosted Audi's domestic market share at the end of May to seven percent from 5.8 percent in April.

In western Europe outside of Germany, Audi said sales were up 12.3 percent during the first half of the year. Sales in the United States rose about 30 percent and Japanese sales were up 18.1 percent, the carmaker said.
Audi's workforce at the end of June was up almost 10 percent over the level in June 1996, rising by about 3,400 workers to 37,400.
